title: Açorda (Alentejo bread soup with garlic, coriander and poached egg)

ingredients.name: stale country bread, torn into pieces (crusts removed)

steps: Pound the garlic with the salt in a mortar until it forms a paste, then work in half of the coriander.
Stir in the olive oil to loosen the paste and transfer it to a large heatproof bowl or tureen.
Add the bread pieces on top of the paste.
Meanwhile, bring the water to a boil in a pan and poach the eggs gently in it for 3 to 4 minutes, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Pour the boiling water from the pan over the bread and let it stand for a couple of minutes, then stir with a fork until the bread has broken down into a soft, thick soup.
Serve in bowls, each topped with a poached egg and the rest of the coriander.

title: Amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (Portuguese clams in garlic, coriander and white wine)

ingredients.name: small clams, soaked in salted water for 1 hour to remove grit

steps: Rinse the clams well and discard any that are open and will not close when tapped.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan with the garlic over low heat for a couple of minutes until fragrant but not coloured.
Add the clams and wine, cover and increase the heat to high.
Cook for 4 to 6 minutes, shaking the pan now and then, until all the clams have opened. Discard any that remain shut.
Add the coriander, lemon juice and black pepper and toss to coat. Taste the broth before adding any salt.
Serve right away with the broth and plenty of crusty bread for mopping it up.

title: Arroz de marisco (Portuguese soupy seafood rice)

ingredients.name: small piri-piri chilli or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes

steps: Soften the onion in the olive oil for about 8 minutes, then add the garlic, tomatoes, bay leaf and chilli and cook for 10 minutes until jammy.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for a minute, then pour in the hot stock and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 8 minutes, then nestle the prawns and clams into the rice.
Cover and cook for another 6 to 8 minutes until the rice is tender but the dish is still soupy, and all clams have opened. Discard any that stay closed.
Season with salt, stir in the coriander and serve at once in deep bowls.

title: Bacalhau à Brás (Portuguese salt cod scrambled with eggs, onions and shoestring potatoes)

ingredients.name: salt cod, soaked for 24 to 36 hours in several changes of cold water, then flaked
potatoes, cut into thin matchsticks (or 150 g good thin potato crisps)

steps: If frying the potatoes yourself, dry the matchsticks well and fry them in hot oil until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the onions gently for about 10 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic and the flaked cod and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, so the cod absorbs the flavours.
Add the potatoes and mix well.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently over low heat until they are just set but still creamy and moist. Take the pan off the heat before the eggs dry out.
Season with plenty of black pepper, adding salt only if needed. Scatter the parsley and olives on top and serve immediately.

title: Bacalhau com natas (Portuguese salt cod baked with potatoes and cream)

ingredients.name: salt cod, soaked for 24 to 36 hours in several changes of water
potatoes, peeled and cut into thin strips or cubes
black pepper and parsley to taste

steps: Simmer the soaked cod in water for 8 to 10 minutes, then drain, remove the skin and bones and flake the fish.
Fry the potato strips in oil until golden and nearly cooked, or boil the cubes until tender, and drain.
Soften the onion and garlic in the olive oil for about 10 minutes.

To make the sauce, melt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk and cream gradually and simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Season with nutmeg and black pepper and a little salt only if needed.
Combine the cod, potatoes and onion in a baking dish and pour the sauce over everything.
Top with the grated cheese and bake at 200 C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Bifana (Portuguese garlic and wine marinated pork sandwich)

ingredients.name: mustard and piri-piri sauce, to serve

steps: Mix the garlic, wine, paprika, bay leaves, vinegar and salt in a bowl, add the pork slices and turn to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the lard in a wide pan over medium-high heat and lift the pork out of the marinade, shaking off the excess but keeping the liquid.
Fry the pork in batches for about 2 minutes per side until lightly browned.
Return all the meat to the pan, add the reserved marinade and simmer for 10 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce has reduced to a glossy coating.
Split the rolls and fill them generously with the pork and its sauce.
Serve warm with mustard or piri-piri sauce on the side.

title: Bolinhos de bacalhau (Portuguese salt cod fritters)

ingredients.name: salt cod, soaked for 24 to 36 hours in several changes of cold water
small onion, grated or very finely chopped

steps: Simmer the soaked cod in water for 8 to 10 minutes, then drain, remove the skin and bones and shred the fish very finely.
Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, then peel and mash them while hot and let the mash cool.
Mix the cod, mash, onion, parsley, nutmeg and pepper, then beat in the eggs one at a time until the mixture is firm but moist. Taste before adding any salt.
Heat the oil to about 180 C in a deep pan.
Using two tablespoons, shape the mixture into oval quenelles and slip them carefully into the oil. Fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot or at room temperature, with a tomato rice or a green salad.

title: Bolo do caco (Madeiran sweet potato flatbread with garlic butter)

ingredients.name: plain flour, or strong white bread flour

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt and add the cooled mashed sweet potato.
Add enough warm water to bring everything together and knead for about 10 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
Cover and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into 6 pieces, shape into balls and flatten each into a disc about 1.5 cm thick. Let them rest for 20 minutes.
Cook on a dry, flat heavy griddle or frying pan over medium-low heat for about 8 to 10 minutes on each side until golden, with a pale ring around the middle.
Mash the butter with the garlic and parsley, split the warm breads and spread generously with the garlic butter.

title: Caldo verde (Portuguese potato and kale soup with chouriço)

ingredients.name: collard greens or kale, stems removed and leaves sliced into very thin strips
chouriço or other smoked sausage, thinly sliced

steps: Put the potatoes, onion, garlic and water in a pot with a little salt and simmer for about 20 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.
Mash the potatoes in the pot, or blend with a hand blender, until the soup is thick and smooth.
Stir in 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and return the pot to a gentle simmer.
Add the shredded greens and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes, so they stay bright green and just tender.
Meanwhile, gently fry the sausage slices in a dry pan until they release their fat and start to crisp.
Taste for salt, ladle into bowls, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and top with the sausage slices.

title: Canja de galinha (Portuguese chicken and rice soup with mint and lemon)

ingredients.name: chicken thighs or drumsticks, bone in
short-grain rice or small soup pasta

steps: Put the chicken, water, onion, carrot, bay leaf and salt in a pot, bring to a boil and skim any foam from the surface.
Cover and simmer gently for 40 to 45 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth, discarding the onion, carrot and bay leaf. Remove the skin and bones and shred the meat.
Return the broth to the pot, bring to a simmer and add the rice. Cook for about 12 to 15 minutes until tender.
Add the shredded chicken and a handful of chopped mint, and warm through.
Finish with lemon juice, adjust the seasoning and serve with a mint sprig on top.

title: Carne de porco à alentejana (Portuguese pork and clams with fried potatoes)

ingredients.name: pork loin or shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
sweet paprika paste, or 2 tsp sweet paprika
small clams, purged in salted water

steps: Mix the pork with the wine, garlic, paprika, bay leaves and a little salt and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Fry the potato cubes in oil until golden and cooked through and drain them on paper towels.
Lift the pork out of the marinade and pat it dry. Brown it well in the lard over medium-high heat in a wide pan.
Pour in the marinade and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce has reduced.
Add the clams, cover the pan and cook for 4 to 6 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Stir in the potatoes and coriander, and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Chanfana (Portuguese goat braised in red wine in a clay pot)

ingredients.name: goat meat on the bone, cut into pieces (mature lamb or mutton also works)
sweet paprika paste, or 2 tsp sweet paprika

steps: Place the goat in a bowl with half the wine, the garlic, bay leaves, paprika, pepper and salt. Mix well and marinate in the refrigerator overnight.
Heat the oven to 160 C.
Transfer the meat and marinade to an ovenproof clay pot or heavy casserole, add the onion, lard and remaining wine.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, stirring once or twice, until the meat is very tender and falling off the bone.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes so the sauce reduces slightly.
Serve hot from the pot with boiled potatoes.

title: Cozido à portuguesa (Portuguese boiled meats, sausage and vegetables)

ingredients.name: pork belly or smoked pork shoulder, in a piece
white cabbage or savoy cabbage, cut into wedges

steps: Put the beef and pork in a large pot, cover with water and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam and simmer, covered, for 1 hour.
Add the chicken and sausage and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Lift out the sausage and chicken and set aside. Add the carrots and turnips to the pot and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage wedges and cook for another 20 minutes until all the vegetables and the meats are tender.
Strain off some of the broth and cook the rice in it with a pinch of salt until tender.
Slice the meats and sausage and arrange them on a large platter with the vegetables, and serve with the rice.

title: Francesinha (Porto sandwich with steak, sausage, ham, cheese and beer sauce)

ingredients.name: thin beef or pork steaks (about 200 g)
linguiça or other smoked sausages, split lengthwise
melting cheese such as Edam or Gouda

steps: For the sauce, soften the onion and garlic in the butter, stir in the flour and tomato paste, then add the beer, stock, brandy, bay leaf and piri-piri.
Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until reduced and thick, remove the bay leaf and season, then keep it hot.
Season the steaks and cook them in a hot pan for 2 to 3 minutes per side. Grill or fry the sausages until cooked through.
Heat the grill. For each sandwich, lay a slice of bread on a heatproof plate, add ham, a steak and sausage, then another slice of bread.
Cover the top of each sandwich with two cheese slices, covering the edges. Grill until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Top each with a fried egg, pour the hot sauce over the sandwich and serve with chips.

title: Ovos moles (Portuguese sweet egg yolk cream from Aveiro)

ingredients.name: wafer shells, or small glasses, to serve

steps: Separate the eggs carefully, keeping the yolks and removing any trace of white, and press the yolks through a fine sieve into a bowl.

Heat the sugar and water in a small pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then boil without stirring for about 5 minutes until the syrup is slightly thick and forms a thin thread when drawn off a spoon (about 105 C).
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 1 minute, then pour the hot syrup in a thin stream into the yolks, whisking constantly.
Return the mixture to a low heat and cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 3 to 5 minutes until it thickens enough to see the base of the pan when you stir.
Let it cool completely, then spoon it into wafer shells or small glasses.
Serve at room temperature, and keep any leftovers refrigerated.

title: Pão de Ló (Portuguese moist sponge cake)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Butter a 22 cm round tin and line it with baking paper.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, sugar, salt and lemon zest with an electric whisk for about 10 minutes until the mixture is pale, very thick and has tripled in volume.
Sift the flour over the egg mixture in three additions, folding in gently with a spatula so the air is not knocked out.
Pour into the tin and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is just set, but still moist and soft inside.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Peixinhos da horta (Portuguese battered fried green beans)

ingredients.name: flat or runner green beans, trimmed
cold water or cold sparkling water

steps: Cook the beans in boiling salted water for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender, then drain and pat them very dry.
Whisk the flour, egg, water and salt into a smooth batter about as thick as double cream.
Heat the oil to about 180 C in a deep pan.
Dip the beans, one or two at a time, into the batter, letting the excess drip off.
Fry in batches for about 2 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with salt and serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Polvo à lagareiro (Portuguese roast octopus with potatoes, garlic and olive oil)

ingredients.name: octopus, cleaned (frozen and thawed is fine)
coarse salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Put the octopus in a large pot with the onion and bay leaves, cover with water, bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for about 45 to 60 minutes until a knife slides easily into the thickest part. Do not salt the water.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Heat the oven to 220 C. Cut the octopus into large pieces and arrange it in a roasting tin with the potatoes.
Crush each potato lightly with the palm of your hand so it splits, scatter over the garlic, and pour on the olive oil. Season with coarse salt and pepper.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes until the octopus tips are crisp and the potatoes are golden, basting once with the oil.
Scatter with coriander and serve straight from the tin.

title: Toucinho do Céu (Portuguese almond and egg yolk cake)

ingredients.name: butter, melted, plus extra for the tin

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Butter and flour a 22 cm round tin.
Bring the sugar, water, cinnamon stick and lemon zest to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes into a light syrup. Remove the cinnamon and let the syrup cool to lukewarm.
Stir the ground almonds into the syrup, then beat in the egg yolks and whole eggs, one at a time, followed by the melted butter.
Return the mixture to a very low heat for a few minutes, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Pour into the tin and bake for about 25 to 30 minutes until the cake is golden and just set.
Cool in the tin, turn out and dust with icing sugar. Serve in small slices as it is rich.
